identification.summary: Pearl Sleet is Microsoft's name for a North Korea-based threat actor [S3][S4][S6]. Community catalogs describe it as a nation-state espionage group, active since at least 2012, that mainly targets North Korean defectors and media organizations [S4][S6].
identification.firstObserved: Community catalogs: active since at least 2012 [S4][S6]. Earliest dated Microsoft public reference found: December 2023 [S5].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Pearl Sleet. Microsoft's public naming feed lists LAWRENCIUM as its other name [S3]. MISP Galaxy and Malpedia also list DEV-0215 [S4][S6]. Microsoft's mapping file does not include DEV-0215 [S3]. No source gathered maps Pearl Sleet to another vendor's cluster (for example APT37/ScarCruft or Kimsuky). Do not merge it with those groups.

attribution.sponsor: North Korea (DPRK). Microsoft lists Pearl Sleet's origin/threat as North Korea [S3]. No public source gathered names a specific DPRK organization (for example RGB or MSS) behind it.
attribution.confidence: Microsoft lists Pearl Sleet as a North Korea-based actor [S3]; community catalogs derived from Microsoft reporting describe it as a North Korean nation-state espionage group [S4][S6]. This is a vendor assessment. No US or ROK government attribution of Pearl Sleet by name was found.
attribution.basis: Microsoft public naming feed [S3]; community catalogs derived from Microsoft reporting [S4][S6].

objectives: Cyber espionage, per community catalogs [S4][S6]. Reported targets point to an interest in the North Korean defector community and media, consistent with regime-security priorities. That last inference is analyst judgment drawn from [S4][S6].

targeting.notes: The defector and media focus comes from community catalogs [S4][S6]. No target region was confirmed in this check.

campaigns.name: Public naming by Microsoft
campaigns.summary: A Microsoft Defender XDR monthly news post (December 2023) is cited by community catalogs as the reference introducing the Pearl Sleet profile.

diamond.adversary: North Korea-based actor tracked by Microsoft as Pearl Sleet (formerly LAWRENCIUM) [S3].
diamond.victim: North Korean defectors and media organizations [S4][S6].

gaps: No public source gathered describes Pearl Sleet's malware, initial-access methods, infrastructure or ATT&CK techniques. Capabilities remain Research Required.

Could not open Microsoft's December 2023 Defender XDR monthly news post (techcommunity.microsoft.com, DNS failure) [S5]. The 'active since 2012' and 'defectors and media' description in community catalogs appears to derive from it but was not verified against the original.

Could not open Microsoft's threat actor naming page (learn.microsoft.com) or the full PDF of the April 2024 East Asia report (go.microsoft.com). Pearl Sleet details beyond the landing page are unverified.
DEV-0215 appears as an alias in MISP Galaxy and Malpedia [S4][S6] but not in Microsoft's public mapping JSON [S3]. Treat it as unconfirmed by Microsoft.

No mapping to other vendor clusters (APT37/ScarCruft/Ruby Sleet, Kimsuky/Emerald Sleet, Konni) was found. Overlap with other DPRK groups targeting defectors is unknown. Do not merge it with those groups.
No MITRE ATT&CK group entry, government advisory, indictment or sanction naming Pearl Sleet was found.
No dated Pearl Sleet-specific activity was confirmed.

Microsoft's April 2024 East Asia report [S1] covers North Korean activity from June 2023, but a fact-check could not confirm from search results that it names Pearl Sleet. Earlier claims citing it (June 2023 targeting of South Korean defector-support and human-rights entities; intelligence-collection motive) were removed pending direct verification.

provenance.importedSummary: Pearl Sleet is a nation state activity group based in North Korea that has been active since at least 2012. They primarily target defectors from North Korea, media organizations in carrying out their cyber espionage activities.
